constraints: Keep the baseline, held-out test split and accuracy measurement unchanged. These fixed evaluation objects do not prohibit changing the treatment classifier cutoff.

Preserve accuracy as a fraction with higher values better, success when treatment accuracy > baseline accuracy, and falsification when treatment accuracy <= baseline accuracy. These comparisons remain fixed while the treatment classifier cutoff changes.

opportunity_statement: The bottleneck is constant majority-class prediction missing minority-class cases; replacing it only in poc_patch.py with a threshold midway between training class means may recover those cases if separation transfers to the held-out split, while preserving the baseline, test split, accuracy calculation and registered comparisons.
risks: Overlapping classes or outlier-sensitive training means could place the midpoint poorly, producing treatment accuracy equal to or below baseline and falsifying the improvement claim.
The tiny authored demonstration may not represent other datasets; three repeats with fixed seed 42 would not establish generalization across independent splits.
summary: In poc_patch.py only, replace majority-class prediction with a cutoff halfway between the two training class means, assigning each side to the corresponding class. If the captured feature separates classes and that relationship persists in the held-out split, this may recover minority-class cases that constant majority prediction misses, yielding more correct predictions overall. Preserve the baseline, test split, accuracy calculation and fixed comparisons.
title: Replace majority prediction with a training-derived midpoint cutoff
